Selected Learning Tracks

From first line of code to a working system.

The path is adjusted to the learner's level. These are the core tracks I use most often — not a rigid one-size-fits-all syllabus.

⚡

Arduino & IoT

Electronics, sensors, motors and embedded programming, progressing toward smart-home and IoT mini-projects.

Recommended from 11+
⌘

Python

Programming foundations, functions, modules, GUI work and project mentoring with an emphasis on clear thinking.

Recommended from 8+
◉

PictoBlox + AI

Block coding, interactive projects and beginner-friendly AI / machine-learning concepts without complex syntax.

Recommended from 7+
▣

MIT App Inventor

Build Android apps visually, then use logic blocks to add real interactivity and data.

Recommended from 9+
⚙

Robotics & LEGO

Mechanical thinking, sensors, control loops, testing and competition-style problem solving.

Recommended from 7+
◇

Fusion 360

Sketching, basic 3D modeling and design thinking for prototyping real parts.

Recommended from 12+
How I Teach

Less passive watching.
More engineering thinking.

01 — DIAGNOSE

Find the real level

Identify what is already understood and what is missing, so time is not wasted repeating basics.

02 — CONCEPT

Make it make sense

Reduce a technical idea to a simple model, then connect it to a real system.

03 — BUILD

Apply it immediately

The learner codes, wires, designs or simulates something small enough to finish and understand.

04 — DEBUG

Explain independently

We troubleshoot failures and finish with the learner explaining the logic in their own words.

Engineering Evidence

I teach from systems I have actually built and debugged.

These are engineering / project examples that support the technical depth behind the tutoring. They are not presented as student projects.

Humanoid robot build

InMoov humanoid robot

A 3D-printed humanoid with mapping, navigation, face detection and voice commands (ROS, OpenCV) — the kind of real debugging I bring into lessons.

Home Automation / IoT session

Home Automation / IoT

A live remote session on a real smart-home setup (ESP32/8266, Blynk / ThingSpeak) — hands-on hardware, not a slide-only lesson.

Competitions & Mentoring

Practice under real constraints.

Competition preparation develops iteration, communication, team problem-solving and the discipline to make a system work under pressure.

FAQ

Good questions before we start.

From ~7 years for block coding (PictoBlox) up to teens and adults for Python, Arduino, IoT and Fusion 360. The track is chosen by level, not just age.

Both. Most tutoring is online (Preply / live sessions); in-person robotics and hardware sessions are possible depending on availability and scope.

For coding tracks: a laptop and internet. For robotics/Arduino tracks I advise on a simple starter kit — we can begin with simulators before buying hardware.

Both — the teaching language adapts to the learner so the concept is understood, not just memorised.

Start from your actual level

If you already know some code, we skip the basics. If you're starting from zero, we build the foundation properly.
